draft.title: Opportunity cost
card: Because resources are limited, choosing one thing means not choosing others. Every choice has something given up.
The opportunity cost of a choice is the next best option you give up. It is only one thing, not a list of everything you missed out on.
Say you spend Saturday at work. Your options were work, time with friends, or sleeping in. If time with friends was your next best choice, that is the opportunity cost.
Opportunity cost is not always money. It can be time, or the use of a resource such as land or a machine.
draft.remember: Opportunity cost is the next best option given up, not everything given up.

a.q: Zoe has $20. She could buy a book, see a movie or buy a cap. She buys the book, and the movie was her next best choice. What is her opportunity cost?
opts: Seeing the movie
Buying the cap
The $20 she spent
Seeing the movie and buying the cap
a.why: Opportunity cost is the next best option given up. The movie was Zoe's next best choice, so it is the cost. The cap was also given up, but it was not the next best, and opportunity cost is only one option.
a.clue: Look for the next best choice, not all the choices.

b.q: Sam's school council owns a spare hall. It could be used for a Year 7 disco, a chess club or a book sale. The council picks the disco. Chess club ranked second and the book sale third. What is the opportunity cost of holding the disco?
opts: Using the hall for the chess club
Using the hall for the book sale
Using the hall for the book sale and chess club
The cost of the disco decorations
b.why: The next best option given up is the chess club, so that is the opportunity cost. The book sale was also given up, but it ranked lower. The cost of decorations is money spent, not the option given up.
b.clue: Pick the second ranked use of the hall.

b.best: Using the hall for the chess club

problems.detail: The clue 'Pick the second ranked use of the hall' plus the stem's 'Chess club ranked second' hands over the answer. A student can match the words without understanding opportunity cost. A clue such as 'Look for the next best use, not all the uses' would avoid this.
